chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Amr ibn al-Ash'as, who heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

The man is questioned in his grave. So if he is firm (in his faith), space is expanded for him in his grave by seven cubits, and a door is opened for him to Paradise, and it is said to him: 'Sleep the sleep of the newly-wed, with delighted eyes.'

key_terms.نَوْمَةَ الْعَرُوس: The sleep of the newly-wed (indicating comfort and bliss)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a believer's grave if they remain firm in their faith after death?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the immediate reward for a steadfast believer following the trial of Munkar and Nakir, emphasizing that spiritual firmness translates into physical comfort in the barzakh. The metaphor of 'sleep of the bride' underscores the profound tranquility and joy experienced by the righteous, contrasting with the distress of the unfaithful. This event serves as a critical link between death and resurrection, affirming the reality of the intermediate realm.
